Hon'Ble Kunal Ravi Singh, J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, Shri Fuzail Ahmand Ansari, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State respondents and Shri Rajesh Kumar Jaiswal, learned counsel appearing for respondent no.1.
2.

The petitioners have preferred this writ petition for the following relief :-
"i. Issue a writ order or direction in the Nature of mandamus directing the respondents to pay the compensation to the petitioners in pursuance of the award dated 08.08.2025 declared by the Competent Authority/ Special Land Acquisition Officer (Joint Organization) Bareilly in respect of Gata No.328 area 0.1582 hectare i.e. 1582 Sq. meter of the revenue Village Saidpurkani, Tehsil Awala, District Bareilly.
ii. Issue a writ order or direction in the Nature of mandamus directing the National Highway Authority to deposit the awarded amount before the Competent Authority within fifteen days. "

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners fairly submits that as the award is likely to be challenged by the Union of India, Ministry of Road Transport and Highway before the Arbitrator under Section 3(G)5 of the National Highways Act, 1956(Act, 1956), only on this account, the respondents had not released the compensation in view of the award dated 08.08.2025.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners has placed reliance on the orders dated 05.08.2025 passed in Writ C No.24521 of 2025 titled as "Dharmveer Mittal Vs. Union of India and 5 others" and Writ C No.25712 of 2024 titled as "Seema Rani and another Vs. Union of India and 4 others" decided on 27.09.2024.

sentences.text: He next submits that in case, the N.H.A.I. has filed any arbitration proceeding in view of the provision contained under section 3(G)5 of the Act, 1956, in such situation, in terms of the successive orders of Division Bench, the petitioners would definitely furnish indemnity bond for the entire amount before the Competent Authority within reasonable time and the compensation, in lieu of the award, be released thereof.
4. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, we are not inclined to keep the matter pending consideration or to invite any counter affidavit.
In the interest of justice, we find that in case, there is no other impediment, the compensation be released in favour of the petitioners.

Needless to say that in case, N.H.A.I. choose to file or challenge the award in appropriate proceedings, in such a situation, in the light of order passed by this Court in aforementioned case,
